verbalization: (+)-Actinidine is implicated in the biological pathway leading to the inhibition of S-methylmethionine--homocysteine S-methyltransferase BHMT2 through a complex network of interactions. The evidence suggests that (+)-Actinidine acts as a target for Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B, which in turn is a target of Oleanolic Acid 3-O-Alpha-Rhamnopyranosyl-(1->3)-Beta-Glucuronopyranosyl28-O-Beta-Glucopyranoside. This chain of targets ultimately points to BHMT2 as the downstream enzyme affected. The integration of these relationships implies that (+)-Actinidine may exert its biological effects through a mechanism involving the modulation of TnF receptor signaling, which could influence the activity of BHMT2. The evidence supports a potential indirect interaction between (+)-Actinidine and BHMT2, mediated through the TnF receptor superfamily member 10B pathway.
